prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots put B008 first, and I do not treat that agreement as proof of merit, so I re-checked the case on its own terms. The chain runs from proglucagon processing and the identification of the insulinotropic truncated peptide, through human incretin physiology, to receptor-targeted drugs with replicated outcome benefit in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease. Few candidates on this list link a basic physiological discovery so directly to a major change in medicine, and independent confirmation is decades deep. The scientific story is also coherent enough to be written as one citation about the peptide and its physiology, which keeps the prize anchored in discovery rather than in a product.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the real weakness. Four credited names exceed the three-person limit, the Mojsov versus Habener question is not settled by the supplied list, and the largest clinical effect came from industrial medicinal chemistry (long-acting analogues) that a basic-physiology trio leaves out. A prize that omits Knudsen risks being read as ignoring the people who made the drug class work, while one that includes her risks crowding out an early peptide discoverer. If the committee cannot defend the boundary between discovery and development, a two-achievement or different configuration might be safer, though I do not currently see a better one.

responses.point: Marie proposed Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B008, treating Knudsen as the representative of long-acting analogue development and regarding Mojsov's credit as contested.
responses.response: I take the concern seriously, but I come out differently. The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has most often rewarded the discovery that opened the field, and Mojsov's identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form is precisely such a step, since without it neither Holst's physiology nor the analogue programmes had the right molecule. Knudsen's work is a major achievement in pharmaceutical development, but it follows from those discoveries and is the more natural subject of other awards. I would change my view only if the committee wants the citation to reach the drugs themselves, and then I would want the discovery and development argument made openly rather than by substituting a name.

responses.point: Thomas ranked B001 (Krainer and Bennett) third and described it as a clean path from splicing mechanism to a cure-like treatment of spinal muscular atrophy, with a coherent two-person allocation.
responses.response: I agree the mechanism-to-therapy arc and the pairing are cleaner than in B008, and that is a real merit. My reservation is scope: nusinersen has been approved for about ten years and the achievement is tied to one disease and one oligonucleotide platform, whereas incretin biology has changed treatment across several disease areas and has the largest outcome evidence. I would keep B001 as a credible later prize rather than rank it above B017 or B034 this year. His point about Singh, Melki and Lefebvre falling outside the credit list is a fair caution that I cannot resolve from the supplied names.

responses.point: Rickard ranked B017 (CAR-T) second with June and Sadelain, and noted that Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is missing from the credited names.
responses.response: I agree with the June and Sadelain core and with the Eshhar problem, which I see as the main obstacle for B017 because a fair allocation would need to address the original concept. My difference is over Rosenberg: I included him in my opening ballot, but I now see that adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a separate line from CAR design, so I would not insist on a third name. I would still hold B017 as the leading alternative, since its clinical maturity in haematological cancers is not in doubt.

responses.point: Abdel placed B034 (optogenetics) second with Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, and pointed out that the credit dispute might delay recognition even though the method is transformative.
responses.response: I share his view of the scientific importance, and I would rank B034 above several clinically mature candidates on originality of impact. But I disagree that a Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann trio is merely a compromise. It omits Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, and the first of these made key biophysical contributions to the channel's characterisation, so I would not call the allocation defensible until the committee agrees on what the citation recognises, the channel or the neuronal tool. Until then B034 remains an alternative and not my preferred prize.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or an early contributor not on the supplied list (for example Habener) has the stronger claim to the identification of the active GLP-1 peptide.
Whether a prize limited to physiology and basic discovery would be accepted as complete without credit for the industrial development of long-acting analogues.
Whether B034 can be assigned to three people without an unacceptable omission, which determines whether it is a real alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted candidate. My documented co-authorship with Rickard Sandberg and others, and my authorship of the spatial transcriptomics paper, do not involve any shortlisted candidate or credited name.
